pocket_scale.name: USB-C Digital Pocket Scale
pocket_scale.description: Credit-card sized digital scale for estate sales. 0.01g precision, USB-C charging.

recommended_products.why_good: Reliable, compact, widely available on Amazon
Higher max weight, good for larger silver pieces
Cheapest option, works fine for basic weight checks

how_to_use_at_estate_sale: Tare (zero) the scale with a small container or piece of paper
Place item on scale, read weight
Compare to benchmarks: teaspoon solid = 15-20g, plated = 8-12g
Record weight in notes for later reference

what_to_look_for.precision_needed: 0.01g is ideal for coins/jewelry, 0.1g sufficient for flatware
what_to_look_for.size: Credit-card size or smaller fits in pocket

magnet_tester.name: Neodymium Magnet
magnet_tester.description: Small strong magnet for silver testing. Fits in pocket.

recommended_products.why_good: Very strong, tiny, fits in pocket

how_to_use: If attracts = steel core, NOT silver (plated or fake)
If no attraction = could be silver OR non-magnetic base metal (brass, nickel silver)
No attraction doesn't prove silver — must check weight + marks too

uv_light.name: UV/Blacklight Pen
uv_light.description: Small UV light for checking fluorescence of certain materials.
use_case: Some plastics fluoresce under UV (helps identify modern reproductions)
Certain gemstones react to UV light
Not as useful for silver specifically, but good general tool

image_annotation.description: When you send me a photo, I can annotate it with red circles/boxes to highlight:

annotation_types.description: Red circle around hallmarks (925, EPNS, maker marks)
annotation_types.example: Circle '925' mark on underside of spoon

annotation_types.description: Red box around wear points showing base metal
annotation_types.example: Box yellow discoloration at fork tine tips

annotation_types.description: Red arrow + label pointing to specific mark with text
annotation_types.example: Arrow from 'Lion Passant' label to walking lion symbol

annotation_types.description: Red circle around date and mint mark on coins
annotation_types.example: Circle '1943' date and 'D' mint mark on quarter

how_it_works: You send me a photo of an item
I analyze the image and identify hallmarks, marks, wear points
I return an annotated version with red circles/boxes/arrows
I also provide text notes about what I found
limitations: Image quality matters — good lighting and close-up shots work best
Hallmarks must be visible in the photo to annotate
I can't physically touch the item — rely on what's visible

notes_system.description: Save notes about items you show me for future reference

note_fields.location: Where you found it (estate sale name, etc.)

how_to_use: Send me a photo of an item
Tell me any marks you see (or I'll identify them)
I'll analyze and return annotated photo + notes
Type +collection to see all saved items

essential_tools_for_estate_sale: Your iPhone with EstateScout skill loaded
Small cloth to wipe items (dirt hides marks)
